newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's Bucaram says supports strike against him.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's Bucaram says supports strike against him.

text.p: Ecuador's President Abdala Bucaram said he supports a general strike that unions plan for Wednesday in protest against him and his government's austerity policies.

"This is a just strike and our government will join the strike. That's why we have given (state workers) a holiday that day, so that they can go out and protest on the streets," Bucaram told local television late on Sunday.
"The government supports a well-organised strike and hopefully it will be successful," he added.
Unions and opposition groups are holding the strike to demand Bucaram's resignation and to protest big price-hikes for public services such as electricity, telephone charges and public transport.
Despite saying he supported the protests, Bucaram added that his government's tough policies were necessary and condemned his political opponents as "conspirators".
"The measures had to be taken because the economic problem is structural," he said.
Bucaram, who won office six months ago on a populist ticket but then imposed an economic austerity programme, has a reputation for eccentric declarations and behaviour.

His past stunts included jumping out of a helicopter dressed as Batman in an election campaign and releasing a rock-and-roll compact disc early in his presidency. He revels in the nickname "El loco" -- "The Madman".
Bucaram's popularity rating has slumped to 12 percent from a rating of 56 percent just after he took office, according to the most recent polls.
Over 600 protestors have been arrested and about 30 people injured in violent student demonstrations against Bucaram's government since January 8.
